title: Dopamine support and treatment context
note: Qualitative circuit illustration. Settings are not clinical stages, percentages of neuron loss, or predicted treatment responses.

steps.title: Complete circuit
steps.caption: Dopamine supports D1 / Go and restrains D2 / No-Go. GPi continuously inhibits the thalamus; GPe inhibits STN.

steps.title: SNc dopamine
steps.caption: SNc supplies dopamine to the striatum. Typical support is retained in this reference condition.

steps.title: Direct pathway
steps.caption: Dopamine supports D1 / Go activity, helping release the thalamic brake for a selected movement.

steps.title: Indirect pathway
steps.caption: Dopamine restrains D2 / No-Go activity. GPe inhibits STN, keeping the indirect pathway at reference.

steps.title: Combined result
steps.caption: Typical dopamine support favors movement through its different effects on Go and No-Go. This is a qualitative reference.

steps.title: Complete circuit
steps.caption: Both pathways are affected by reduced dopamine. This complete circuit stays in that state while we follow one causal route.

steps.title: SNc dopamine
steps.caption: Loss of dopamine-producing neurons in SNc reduces dopamine signaling to the striatum. Both pathways are affected.

steps.title: Direct pathway
steps.caption: Less D1 support means less Go inhibition of GPi. The direct route therefore contributes to an increased thalamic brake.

steps.title: Indirect pathway
steps.caption: Less D2 restraint raises No-Go activity. GPe falls; STN excites GPi more; the indirect route strengthens the brake.

steps.title: Combined result
steps.caption: Both routes increase GPi inhibition of the thalamus. Less excitation returns to cortex. This setting is qualitative, not a clinical stage.

steps.title: Precursor
steps.caption: L-DOPA is a precursor used for dopamine replacement. It can cross the blood-brain barrier.

steps.title: Conversion
steps.caption: In the brain, L-DOPA is converted into dopamine, supporting dopamine signaling.

steps.title: Possible effects
steps.caption: Possible side effects include drug-induced hyperkinesia and cognitive impairment from effects on other dopamine pathways.

steps.title: Pulse generator
steps.caption: Deep brain stimulation uses an implanted electrode connected to a pulse generator.

steps.title: Target region
steps.caption: A common target in this lecture is STN: the subthalamic nucleus. Globus pallidus and thalamus are alternatives.

steps.title: Circuit effect
steps.caption: Stimulation changes activity in the target region and wider circuit. The lecture describes reducing abnormal STN activity.

steps.title: Adaptive feedback
steps.caption: Adaptive DBS adds feedback about the current context, instead of keeping stimulation constant.

steps.title: Adjustment
steps.caption: Feedback about the current context informs an adjustment to stimulation. The circuit then supplies further feedback.
